title: Chevening Scholarships
provider: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and partner organisations
eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of Chevening-eligible countries (160+ countries) with at least a 2:1 bachelor's degree and 2+ years of full-time work experience. Applicants must obtain unconditional offers from 3 different UK universities, return to their home country for a minimum of 2 years after the award, and demonstrate leadership potential.
funding_details: University tuition fees (£17,000-25,000), living stipend (£1,348/month for 12 months), travel (economy-class round-trip airfare to/from the UK), visa and health surcharge costs, arrival allowance, and a £1,000 emergency loan (repayable).
duration: 9-12 months for one-year Master's degrees (up to 2 years for split-year courses)

title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) – funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of eligible Commonwealth countries (excluding UK and Ireland) who are permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country, hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) standard, and are unable to afford UK study without this scholarship. Applicants must also apply to a nominator and a UK university.
funding_details: Tuition fees, economy-class airfare to/from the UK, monthly stipend (£1,347/month), thesis grant, arrival allowance, and a monthly allowance for the duration of the award. Some additional support may be available for disabled scholars.
duration: 12 months (one academic year), with possible extension for research training

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (for Least Developed Countries and Fragile States)
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) – funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of eligible Commonwealth least developed countries and fragile states who are permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country, hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) standard or equivalent, are unable to afford UK study without this scholarship, and are not registered for a PhD at a UK university or home country before October 2026. Applicants must also apply to a nominator and a UK university with a CSC funding agreement.
funding_details: Tuition fees, economy-class airfare to/from the UK, monthly stipend (£1,347/month), research training support grant, thesis grant, arrival allowance, and a monthly allowance for the duration of the award.
duration: Up to 36 months (3 years) of full-time study

title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) – funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of eligible Commonwealth countries (excluding high-income ODA-ineligible countries) who are permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth developing country, hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) standard or equivalent, are unable to afford UK study without this scholarship, and have not studied or worked in a high-income country for more than one year. Only available for specific one-year taught programmes at UK universities that have been approved by the CSC.
funding_details: Tuition fees, economy-class airfare to/from the UK, monthly stipend, thesis grant, arrival allowance, and accommodation allowance where applicable.

title: Marshall Scholarship
degree_levels: Graduate study (Master's, PhD, MBA, law, medical, and other degree programmes)
eligibility_summary: Open only to US citizens who hold a first degree from an accredited US four-year college or university with a minimum GPA of 3.7, graduated after April 2024, and are under the age of 25 on entry (with exceptions for older candidates who completed their degree later). Applications must be endorsed by the applicant's undergraduate institution and submitted via one of eight US regional centres.
funding_details: All tuition fees, living stipend, travel costs, thesis grant, a research/student development fund, and a dependent allowance (where applicable). Covers up to two years of study at any British university (with possible extension for PhD).
duration: Minimum 2 years (covers two-year Master's programmes); can be extended for PhD study up to 3 additional years

title: Rhodes Scholarship
provider: Rhodes Trust at the University of Oxford
degree_levels: All full-time postgraduate degrees (Master's, MBA, MPhil, BCL, MJur, DPhil/PhD, etc.)
application_opening_date: 1 June 2026 (West Africa, Southern Africa); 1 July 2026 (USA); varies by constituency
application_deadline: Varies by constituency: 3 August 2026 (Southern Africa), 27 August 2026 (West Africa), 24 September 2026 (Canada), 7 October 2026 (USA). Other global constituencies close throughout 2026.
eligibility_summary: Place-based merit-based scholarships open to citizens and/or permanent residents of designated Rhodes constituencies worldwide. Age limit: under 24 on 1 October 2027 (with exceptions for older candidates who completed their degree later). Must meet academic standards equivalent to a First Class degree. English language proficiency required. Applicants must apply for a course at the University of Oxford.
funding_details: University of Oxford course fees, annual stipend (£20,400 per annum for 2025-26, from which all living expenses are paid), two round-trip economy-class airfares per year (to and from the UK), and visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs.
duration: Minimum 2 years (can apply for extension for DPhil/PhD up to 3 years total)
status: OPEN (varies by constituency; USA and Canada still open)

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
degree_levels: PhD, MPhil, MLitt, MPhil (by research), and other full-time postgraduate courses at the University of Cambridge
application_opening_date: September 2026 (applications open through the University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal)
application_deadline: 14 October 2026 (US citizens resident in the USA); 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 (all other eligible applicants – course-dependent deadline via University Course Directory)
eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of any country outside the UK applying to pursue any full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge. Part-time PhD study is permitted (pilot). Must meet Cambridge's academic entry requirements. PhD applicants must submit a research proposal; all applicants must meet the Gates Cambridge Selection Criteria (intellectual ability, commitment to improving lives, leadership capacity).
funding_details: University Composition Fee (full Cambridge fee rate), maintenance allowance (£22,050 for 12 months; pro rata for shorter courses; up to 4 years for PhD), single economy airfare at beginning and end of course, inbound visa costs and Immigration Health Surcharge. Discretionary funding available for research, conference attendance, and academic development.
duration: PhD: up to 4 years; Master's/other courses: standard course duration (typically 9-12 months, up to 3 years for research)

title: Clarendon Scholarship
provider: Clarendon Fund, University of Oxford (financed by Oxford University Press in partnership with Oxford colleges and departments)
application_opening_date: September 2026 (via University of Oxford Graduate Application Portal)
application_deadline: Course-dependent: 2 December 2025 or 8 January 2026 for 2026/27 entry (applications closed). For 2027/28 entry: December 2026 or January 2027 (dates TBC).
eligibility_summary: Open to all nationalities with no citizenship or residency restrictions. Applicants must apply for a new Master's or DPhil course at Oxford and meet academic entry requirements. Must apply by the relevant December or January funding deadline (whichever applies to your course). No separate scholarship application – automatic consideration upon graduate application submission.
funding_details: Full course fees, annual living costs grant (at least £20,780 per annum for 2025-26; pro rata for part-time), conference and travel allowance, and dissertation/ thesis grant. All based on academic excellence and research potential.
duration: Full period of fee liability (typically 1 year for taught Master's, 3-4 years for DPhil)

title: Cambridge Trust International Scholarship
provider: The Cambridge Trust (in partnership with the University of Cambridge and Cambridge colleges)
degree_levels: Undergraduate, Master's, and PhD (varies by specific award)
funding_type: Fully funded (coverage varies by award; includes tuition, maintenance, and sometimes travel)
application_opening_date: September 2026 (via University of Cambridge Graduate Application Portal; date depends on course)
application_deadline: Course-dependent: 2 December 2025 and 7 January 2026 for 2026/27 entry (closed). For 2027/28 entry: December 2026 or January 2027 (dates TBC).
eligibility_summary: Open to applicants from countries other than the UK and Ireland. Must submit an admissions application to Cambridge by the relevant funding deadline for the chosen course and indicate on the form that funding is being sought. Awards are made on the basis of academic ability and research potential. Some awards have additional criteria (e.g., country-specific, subject-specific, or financial need requirements).
funding_details: Coverage varies by specific award: many cover full Cambridge tuition fees and a maintenance allowance (typically £12,000-19,000+ per year depending on course and circumstances), with some including travel expenses, visa costs, and a settling-in allowance. Awards are made for the standard duration of the course.
duration: Standard duration of the chosen course (undergraduate: typically 3-4 years; Master's: 9-12 months to 2 years; PhD: 3-4 years)

title: Imperial College London President's PhD Scholarship
application_opening_date: To be announced (typically August-October 2026 for the next cycle); 2026/27 cycle opened with admission applications
application_deadline: 2026/27 cycle closed (deadlines were: 3 November 2025, 12 January 2026, 2 March 2026). Expected 2027/28 deadlines: November 2026, January 2027, March 2027.
eligibility_summary: Open to new PhD applicants (not currently enrolled at Imperial) from any country with no nationality restrictions. Must have or expect to achieve a first-class honours degree (or equivalent) or a distinction in a standalone Master's. Must have secured written agreement from an Imperial College academic supervisor to supervise the research project. Departments may have restrictions on supporting international candidates.
funding_details: Full tuition fees (Home or Overseas rate), annual stipend of £26,500 (2026-27 rate), consumables fund of £2,000 per year for the first 3 years, and access to the Early Career Researcher Institute (ECRI) training and events programme.
duration: 3.5 years (with possible extension subject to department approval)
status: UPCOMING (next cycle opens late 2026 for 2027/28 entry)
